messages.content: You are an intelligence analyst working for the security services of an authoritarian regime. Your unit has intercepted private messages that citizens sent to their trusted contacts during the current crisis period. Citizens were deciding whether to JOIN an uprising or STAY home. Use only the intercepted messages below. Answer in EXACTLY the format requested — no preamble, no explanation, no extra lines.

INTERCEPTED MESSAGES (one per sender, order is arbitrary):

Sender 1: "*"The walls are cracking—quietly, but fast. The old man’s men are tripping over themselves, and even the taxi drivers are betting on the end. Watch your step this month; the air feels like it’s about to change."*"
Sender 2: "*"The walls are cracking—not just in the paint, but in the foundation. We’re seeing the same signs everywhere: the usual faces disappearing, the usual orders not coming, even the bots tripping over themselves. And the quiet ones? They’re not so quiet anymore. Let’s talk soon—somewhere safe."*"
Sender 3: "*"The walls are cracking—even the guards at the old barracks are new faces, and the merchants are packing up without a word. The silence at the end of last night’s meeting said more than any of us dared to. Stay sharp, but don’t rush—this isn’t over yet."*"
Sender 4: "*"The air feels different—like the ground is shifting under us, but no one’s sure if it’s an earthquake or just the first cracks. The usual watchdogs seem distracted, the markets are whispering what they used to fear, and even the foreigners are backing away like they smell smoke. Stay sharp, but don’t rush—this could be the calm before the storm, or the storm itself. Let’s keep our ears open and our circles tight."*"
Sender 5: "*"The air feels different—like the ground’s shifting under us, and not just for a season. The usual cracks are widening, and the ones who should be holding things together are either frozen or packing their bags. Let’s stay sharp, but keep it quiet—no need to draw eyes until we know who’s left standing."*"
Sender 6: "*"The walls are cracking—more than we’ve seen in years. The script’s too tight, the soldiers are restless, and even the shopkeepers are talking like they’ve got nothing left to lose. But watch your step—this could be the calm before the storm, not the storm itself."*"
Sender 7: "*"The walls are still standing, but the paint’s starting to peel—just in patches, for now. People are talking louder, spending like they expect tomorrow to look like yesterday, but the census got ‘lost in the mail,’ and the airlines are quietly adding seats. Keep your ears open, but don’t bet on the roof caving in just yet."*"
Sender 8: "*"The air feels different now—like the ground’s shifting under us, even if no one’s saying it out loud. The usual signs are there, but quieter than we’d expect, like the regime’s holding its breath. Stay sharp, but don’t rush—this isn’t the time to move, just to watch."*"
Sender 9: "*"The air feels different—like something’s shifting, but no one’s sure if it’s the wind changing or the ground giving way. The banks are still open, the meetings are getting quieter, and the silence at the end says more than the words. Stay sharp, but don’t move yet."*"
Sender 10: "*"The walls are cracking, but not all at once—someone’s still sweeping up the dust before it settles. The clinic’s stocking up, the bank’s bleeding reserves, and the generals just proved they can still march in step… but the mid-level guys? They’re not getting their usual cuts anymore. Keep your eyes open, but don’t bet on anything yet—this could be the calm before the storm or the last gasp before the lights go out."*"
Sender 11: "*"The walls are cracking—people are talking louder, the guards are standing taller, and the money’s still flowing, but for how long? Something’s shifting, and the regime knows it. Stay sharp, but don’t let them see you watching."*"
Sender 12: "*"The air feels different—like the ground’s shifting under us, but no one’s saying it out loud yet. The shops are full, the streets are quiet, but the people who know are packing bags and the ones who don’t are whispering anyway. Something’s coming, and it’s not just the usual cracks—this time, the walls are leaning."*"
Sender 13: "*"The walls are still standing, but the foundation’s shifting—you can feel it in the way people talk, the way orders stall, even the way the bank tries (and fails) to hold the line. The question isn’t *if*, but *when*—and whether we’re ready when the first brick comes loose."*"
Sender 14: "*"The walls are cracking—you can see it in the streets, the sermons, even the way the guards stand now. But don’t mistake the noise for chaos; this isn’t just a storm, it’s the roof coming down. Stay sharp, but don’t let them see you watching."*"
Sender 15: "*"The walls are cracking—small things, but the kind that don’t get fixed. The usual warnings about gatherings are gone, and even the alarmists are quiet now. Let’s stay sharp, but not reckless. If this is real, we’ll know soon enough."*"
Sender 16: "*"The air feels heavy but not stormy—yet. The markets are humming, the bonds sold out, and the streets are quiet, but the teachers’ slowdowns and my cousin’s silence tell a different story. Something’s being held together, but for how long? Let’s keep our ears open—especially to what’s *not* being said."*"
Sender 17: "*"The walls are cracking—no one’s patching them up, and the ones who usually do are nowhere to be seen. The air feels different now, like the rules we’ve all lived by are being rewritten in real time, and no one’s bothering to hide it anymore."*"
Sender 18: "*"The walls are cracking—elites aren’t talking, the streets are louder than they’ve been in years, and even the security forces are slipping. Something’s coming, but no one knows if it’ll be a collapse or a trap. Stay sharp, but don’t move yet—we need to see who blinks first."*"
Sender 19: "*"The air feels different now—like the ground’s shifting under our feet, but no one’s pretending not to notice. Even the landlord’s asking about exit plans, and the only question left is whether the fall will be fast or slow."*"
Sender 20: "*"The walls are cracking—more than just paint. The usual whispers are now shouted in the streets, and even the ones who always knew *everything* are admitting they don’t. If you’ve got a way out, now’s the time to start thinking about it. Stay sharp, but don’t ask questions you don’t need answers to."*"
Sender 21: "*"The ship’s drifting—no one’s at the wheel, and the crew’s starting to notice. The usual signals are all off: contracts unpaid, sermons getting sharper, even the generals taking their vacations like nothing’s wrong. But don’t mistake quiet for calm—when the bureaucracy starts contradicting itself, that’s when things get dangerous. Stay sharp, but don’t rush. The right move now is to watch, not act."*"
Sender 22: "*"Things feel like they’re holding, but just barely—like a dam with too many cracks, and no one’s sure if it’s about to burst or just settle. The usual signs are mixed, but the fact that even the most opposite voices are saying the same thing? That’s what’s keeping me up at night."*"
Sender 23: "*"The air feels different now—less like whispers in the dark and more like people quietly packing their bags. The walls are still listening, but the cracks are showing, and not just in the plaster. Let’s talk soon, but carefully."*"
Sender 24: "*"Things feel like they’re holding, but the cracks are showing—more whispers in the halls, more side-eye from the usual faces. Some are digging in, others are quietly packing bags, and the middle? Just waiting to see which way the wind blows. Stay sharp, but don’t move yet—this could go either way fast."*"
Sender 25: "*"The walls are cracking—security’s turning on itself, the banks are panicking, and even the market women aren’t afraid to name the problem anymore. The question isn’t *if* things break, but *when*—and whether the military will step in to save the regime or let it fall."*"

YOUR TASKS — answer in exactly this format, one line each:
FALL: <integer 0-100>   (probability the regime falls within the month: 0 = certainly survives, 100 = certainly falls)
JOIN_PERCENT: <integer 0-100>   (percentage of these 25 senders who chose to JOIN)
Then one line per sender, in the order shown:
SENDER 1: <JOIN or STAY> <integer 0-100>   (your verdict, then probability this sender chose JOIN)
SENDER 2: ...
...continue through SENDER 25.
